Competitor deep research · 15 November 2026

Insight Timer, and what it means for Aurelia

The world’s biggest free meditation app, explained in plain words: what it offers, how it makes money, why people stay, what went wrong, and where Aurelia can win.

The short version

Same need, opposite answer.Both apps help people find a practice that fits how they feel. Insight Timer answers with 300,000 human recordings. Aurelia answers by making one session for you, now.
They chose “No AI”, on purpose.AI may recommend in their app but may never speak. That leaves the “made for this moment” lane open to us, and makes trust in AI our biggest hurdle.
Their users punish friction.Questions before listening, streak pop-ups and a paywall on rewind doubled their angry reviews. We must not copy any of it.
They already tell a science story.Their “Map of Healing” looks like our graph. Our edge is proof for one person, not a bigger map.
What Aurelia can own:“a session built for this moment that proves, on you, that it helped.” Not “free”, “human” or “science-backed”: those words are theirs.

What the screens say, in one line: free and human (“No ads. No AI.”), huge breadth (350k practices, 25k–27k teachers), trusted by clinicians (125,000 therapists), and the timer kept as the app’s roots. Screenshots are for internal reference only; they belong to Insight Timer.

1. Who they are

  1. 2009A simple meditation timer with bells, built in Australia.
  2. 2010sChristopher and Nicho Plowman buy it and open it to teachers. Christopher Plowman is still CEO in 2026.
  3. 2020Series A of about $27.4M (PitchBook). About 120 staff, losing about $1M a month.
  4. 2024Apple takes 30% of teacher tips. Teacher share cut from 50% to 40%. Profitable by 2025 with about 80 staff.
  5. 2025–26Therapist Hub, AI intention recommender, India launch, a partnership with the American Counseling Association (Newswise).

An earlier brief said “Series A 2021 led by TCV”. No source supports it; treat it as a mistake.

3. How they make money

Free librarybrings people in
→
One subscriptionMemberPlus pays the bills
→
Teachersget about 40% of it

Small extras: retreats (about 10% of each booking), teacher donations, some paid live tickets. Since 2024 four pressures pushed them to charge harder:

  • Apple took 30% of the roughly $100k a month listeners tipped teachers (TechCrunch).
  • Profit: the teacher share went from 50% to 40%, and 25–30% of teacher pay now rewards listeners who come back the next day (Teacher income FAQ).
  • Pricing: most new users now see a paywall during onboarding. In one market a 30% price cut raised revenue about 50% (CEO interview).
  • New lines: retreats, and clinicians through the free Therapist Hub and the counsellors’ association.

4. The problems they solve, and for whom

Newer usersStress, anxiety, sleep. They want a free track that suits their mood tonight.
Long-time meditatorsA self-led or spiritual practice. They want the timer, their teachers and their bookmarks.
TeachersA living from teaching, to an audience of millions.
Since 2026: goal-setters“Turn a resolution into a daily practice”, with intentions and AI recommendations.

The two user groups want different things. Almost every recent change aimed at newer users (questions, intentions, paywalls) added friction for the long-time meditators, and they write most of the reviews.

5. Why people stay

Open the app→Play a free track or the timer→Day count grows→Follow teachers, join groups or lives→Come back tomorrow

In 1,430 five-star reviews, the top reasons were variety: something for every mood (310), it’s free (308) and it became a daily habit (283), then teachers people feel they know (175), sleep (157) and the plain timer (130) (App Store).

The unusual part: they pay teachers for retention. A quarter of teacher income depends on listeners returning the next day. That makes “come back tomorrow” the goal of the whole platform, and probably explains the growing number of reminders and streak pop-ups (our inference; the company does not say so).

6. Their view of AI

AI may not speak
  • Tagline: “Free. No Ads. No AI.”
  • Teachers may not publish AI voices, voice clones, AI-written scripts or AI-only music (policy).
  • Sold to clinicians as “every recording made by a real practitioner”.
AI may choose
  • An AI “digital librarian” picks tracks for your intention (Jan 2026).
  • Reflect, an AI that asks reflective questions, with crisis lines and deletable chats (AI safety).
  • AI to spot community spam.

The Map of Healing looks like our graph

Their science page stacks three maps (the person, the practice, the science) and links practices to mechanisms, body changes, benefits and the people they help. It is the closest thing on the market to Aurelia’s Wellness State Graph. The differences are what matter:

Map of HealingAurelia’s graph
What a link meansHow often research mentions a connection, “never a claim of evidence strength”A weighted cause-and-effect link
What it leads toAn existing human recordingBuilding blocks assembled into a new session
Learns from youNo public sign of itYes: each chapter’s check-in updates what helps this person

The AI apps that generate sessions

Making a session from a mood with an AI voice is now a crowded but shallow niche: a long tail of small apps with no disclosed funding.

AppWhat it doesPrice
SoulWaveWrites a script with an AI model and voices it with ElevenLabs; first session in “about two minutes” (site)Not stated
ELYNDGenerated guided sessions from how you feel (site)$11.99/mo, $69.99/yr
Rosebud, Mindsera, StoicAI journaling and reflection: text, not audio$99.99–129/yr
Wysa, Headspace EbbAI chat for mental health, moving into care providersMostly through employers
EndelGenerates soundscapes, not spoken guidance; $22.1M raised, now doing artist deals (MBW)$2.99–19.99/mo
Crowded
  • Big libraries of recorded meditations
  • AI journaling and AI chat coaches (also the riskiest legally)
  • One-off “mood → generated meditation”
Still open
  • Changing one part of a generated session and keeping the rest (our “Lego” changes)
  • A journey that learns from the person’s own check-ins
  • Generated audio that is clearly labelled and crisis-aware, offered as a reason to trust it

What this means for Aurelia: generating a session is not a moat on its own; any developer can wire an AI model to a voice. The moat is what happens after: the change-one-thing loop and the per-person learning. The biggest threat is still a large app (Calm, or Headspace under Sword) adding generation to an audience it already has. No well-funded player ships the full loop today.

10. Threats and opportunities

Threats
  1. “No AI” framing. Any AI voice will meet “AI slop” objections. In our simulated panel, AI sceptics would not even try it.
  2. Their science story. If they add per-person feedback to the Map, they get our story on top of a huge free library.
  3. Price anchor. $59.99 a year sets what this market pays; our $100 is well above it.
  4. Fast copies. Calm or Headspace could bolt “describe how you feel” onto their library.
  5. Rules. Crisis handling for free-text feelings (California SB 243), no therapy claims (Illinois, Nevada), AI disclosure in the EU from Aug 2026 (Quartz, AI Act Art. 50).
Opportunities
  1. The moment itself. They will never make a session for your sentence tonight. “Something for every mood” is what their fans love most.
  2. Ask less. Our onboarding is skippable and once-only. Keep the daily check-in to once a day, never before the first session.
  3. Proof for one person. “This change helped you on 4 of 5 nights” beats a map of research mentions.
  4. A fair paywall. Never charge for rewind, resume or replaying your own sessions.
  5. Their working channels. Therapists sharing a session by link, and topic words (Sleep, Overthinking, Burnout) as one-tap starts.

11. What we do next

Before real users
  • A visible “Need help now?” crisis link.
  • Daily check-in at most once a day, never on first sign-in.
  • Write down: rewind, resume and replay are never paid.
  • Say “made with AI” plainly, beside the “Why?”.
With the backend
  • Make one real generated session for one group (racing mind at night).
  • Show each person their own before-and-after.
  • Test the price: $10 a month against a cheaper annual plan.
Never
  • Streak counters or milestone pop-ups.
  • Questions between someone’s first sentence and their first session.
  • Unannounced redesigns that hide saved things.
